stimulus.text: The photograph, taken in September 1957, shows a student of the Little Rock Nine arriving at Central High School in Little Rock, Arkansas, escorted by soldiers of the 101st Airborne Division. Governor Orval Faubus had used the Arkansas National Guard to block nine Black students from entering the school. President Dwight D. Eisenhower then federalized the National Guard and sent about 1,000 paratroopers to enforce the federal court order. In the same month, Congress passed the Civil Rights Act of 1957, the first federal civil rights law since Reconstruction.

stem: The soldiers in the photograph were sent to Little Rock mainly to do which of the following?

options.text: Enforce a federal court order desegregating Central High School
Arrest the nine Black students for entering the school
options.misconception: Background from the books: the soldiers escorted the students into school, so they did not arrest them.

options.text: Close the school for the rest of the year
options.misconception: Background from the books: the school stayed open with the students inside, so it was not closed for the year.

options.text: Protect Governor Faubus from protesters outside the school
options.misconception: Background from the books: the troops were sent against Faubus's defiance, not to protect him.

rationales.A: The jeep's 101st Airborne markings and the escorted student show federal troops enforcing the court order.
rationales.B: The soldiers escorted the students into school, so they did not arrest them.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the school stayed open with the students inside, so it was not closed for the year.
rationales.D: The troops were sent against Faubus's defiance, not to protect him.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows a student walking to Central High School beside helmeted soldiers.
2. The stimulus says Faubus used the National Guard to block the nine students.
3. Eisenhower then federalized the Guard and sent about 1,000 paratroopers to enforce the federal court order.
Remember: soldiers escorting students into a school are enforcing a court order, not closing the school.
